articles.title: Emissão online da CIPTEA facilita rotina de pessoas autistas em Macaé | G1
articles.standfirst: Carteira pode ser solicitada pela internet, com acompanhamento do pedido e acesso à versão digital. O serviço é gratuito.
articles.summary: Carteira pode ser solicitada pela internet, com acompanhamento do pedido e acesso à versão digital. O serviço é gratuito.
articles.body:
Sistema online otimiza e centraliza todas as etapas do pedido do documento — Foto: Arquivo Secom

A Prefeitura de Macaé disponibiliza uma plataforma online para a emissão da Carteira de Identificação da Pessoa com Transtorno do Espectro Autista (CIPTEA). O serviço é gratuito e visa otimizar o tempo das famílias de pessoas autistas, permitindo solicitar o documento, acompanhar a análise do pedido e acessar a versão digital pelo celular ou computador, sem a necessidade de comparecimento presencial para dar entrada no processo.

Com a implantação da ferramenta, o procedimento anterior — que permitia o envio de solicitações pelo antigo e-mail institucional — foi totalmente encerrado. A mudança tem como objetivo tornar o atendimento mais organizado, seguro e eficiente, centralizando todas as etapas em um único ambiente digital. O sistema foi desenvolvido pela Secretaria Municipal de Ciência, Tecnologia e Inovação, em parceria com a Secretaria Municipal de Desenvolvimento Social, Direitos Humanos, Acessibilidade e Economia Solidária (SEMDES).

A plataforma conta com mecanismos rigorosos de proteção de dados sensíveis, passando por auditorias constantes e testes nas ferramentas para evitar qualquer risco de vazamento de informações, mantendo o acesso estritamente restrito. A iniciativa representa uma modernização dos serviços públicos e uma facilidade para os usuários, que acompanham a liberação da solicitação à distância, reforçando a acessibilidade, a inclusão e a proteção social no município.

Para os familiares e responsáveis por pessoas autistas, a facilidade de realizar o processo pela internet proporciona um ganho expressivo de tempo no dia a dia. A possibilidade de efetuar o cadastro e o envio de documentos do próprio celular ou computador ajuda quem não tem com quem deixar a criança, permitindo fazer a solicitação de casa, do trabalho ou até mesmo na sala de espera de atendimentos de saúde e terapias.

A CIPTEA possui validade em todo o território nacional e ajuda a garantir direitos previstos em lei, como o atendimento prioritário. Em Macaé, a carteira foi instituída pelo Decreto Municipal nº 007/2020, em conformidade com a Lei Federal nº 13.977/2020 (Lei Romeo Mion).

Para solicitar o documento, o cidadão deve acessar o portal ciptea.macae.rj.gov.br, preencher os dados solicitados, anexar a documentação exigida acompanhada de uma foto recente e acompanhar a análise do pedido diretamente pelo site. Após a aprovação, a versão digital pode ser baixada. Para aqueles que preferirem obter a carteira física, é possível solicitar a opção na própria plataforma e seguir as orientações disponíveis para a retirada presencial do documento impresso.

articles.title: Diesel mais caro pressiona o agro e o frete; entenda | G1
articles.standfirst: Medida mantém benefício de R$ 2,12 por litro em meio à alta do petróleo. Dependência de importações e transporte rodoviário ampliam os efeitos do diesel caro sobre fretes, produção e preços dos alimentos.
articles.summary: Medida mantém benefício de R$ 2,12 por litro em meio à alta do petróleo. Dependência de importações e transporte rodoviário ampliam os efeitos do diesel caro sobre fretes, produção e preços dos alimentos.
articles.body:
O governo federal prorrogou nesta terça-feira (27), por mais 30 dias, o subsídio ao diesel, mantendo o benefício em R$ 2,12 por litro. A medida busca conter os efeitos da alta dos preços internacionais do petróleo , principal matéria-prima do combustível, pressionados pelos conflitos no Oriente Médio e pela guerra entre Rússia e Ucrânia.

O barril do petróleo Brent, referência internacional, foi negociado entre US$ 100 e US$ 106 na primeira quinzena de outubro e chegou a US$ 113,17 no dia 22. Para o governo, qualquer valor acima dos US$ 70 gera pressão forte nos preços para o mercado interno.

Além da alta da commodity, a desvalorização do real também pode encarecer a produção e a importação de diesel. Apesar de ser um grande produtor de petróleo, o Brasil importa cerca de um quinto do diesel que consome, segundo dados da Agência Nacional do Petróleo (ANP).

Em agosto, o diesel importado correspondeu a 23,14% das vendas nacionais de diesel A, combustível ainda sem a mistura obrigatória de biodiesel.

A junção desses fatores dá no seguinte resultado:

O preço do diesel comum subiu 6,67% na primeira quinzena de outubro , chegando à média de R$ 7,20 por litro, segundo o Índice de Preços Edenred Ticket Log (IPTL). Já o diesel S-10 ficou 5,07% mais caro no período, chegando a R$ 7,46 por litro. Em relação a janeiro, o diesel comum acumulou aumento de 15,2%.

Os preços também variam entre as regiões do país. No Norte, o litro do diesel comum custava, em média, R$ 7,75, enquanto o S-10 tinha preço médio de R$ 7,80. Em Roraima, o diesel comum chegou a R$ 8,19; no Acre, o S-10 atingiu R$ 8,30. No Sul e no Sudeste, a média do diesel comum era de R$ 6,97 por litro.

Esse aumento que se reflete no transporte de cargas, feito principalmente por caminhões no Brasil. No agronegócio, o combustível mais caro eleva o custo do frete e da produção, e esse aumento pode ser repassado aos preços dos alimentos.

Como mostrou o Globo Rural , agricultores do Rio Grande do Sul já demonstram preocupação com a possível falta de diesel às vésperas do plantio da safra de verão.

Por que o Brasil precisa importar diesel?

Entre janeiro e agosto, a produção de diesel pela Petrobras chegou a crescer 18,5%, passando de 32,7 milhões para 38,7 milhões de barris. Ainda assim, a produção nacional não foi suficiente para atender a toda a demanda pelo combustível.

No primeiro semestre de 2026, o Brasil consumiu 213,2 milhões de barris de diesel. Segundo a ANP, a produção nacional foi de 154,8 milhões de barris , enquanto as importações somaram 43,5 milhões de barris , o equivalente a 20,4% do consumo no período.

A dependência de importações está relacionada à capacidade de refino do país. Isso porque extrair petróleo não é o mesmo que produzir combustíveis: o petróleo precisa ser processado em refinarias para se transformar em diesel e outros derivados usados por caminhões, máquinas agrícolas e veículos.

Nos últimos anos, a Petrobras vendeu refinarias para empresas privadas como parte de um programa de venda de ativos. Esse movimento ganhou força durante o governo de Jair Bolsonaro (PL), quando a estatal negociou unidades do setor de refino.

O professor Paulo Feldmann, da Faculdade de Economia, Administração, Contabilidade e Atuária da Universidade de São Paulo (FEA-USP), questiona os custos de produção do diesel nessas refinarias e afirma que, em algumas situações, o combustível produzido no Brasil chega a ser mais caro que o importado.

Já Francismar Ferreira, do Instituto de Estudos Estratégicos de Petróleo, Gás Natural e Biocombustíveis (Ineep), afirma que diminuir a dependência das importações exige ampliar e modernizar as refinarias brasileiras, além de rever os investimentos da Petrobras no setor.

Por que a alta do diesel pesa tanto no Brasil?

🕰️ A partir da segunda metade do século XX, o Brasil passou a priorizar o transporte de cargas por rodovias, enquanto as ferrovias perderam espaço. Essa mudança acompanhou o crescimento da indústria automobilística e a expansão da malha rodoviária.

Hoje, a dependência das estradas faz com que a alta do diesel aumente os custos do frete e, consequentemente, do transporte de mercadorias.

“Os combustíveis em geral, sobretudo gasolina e diesel, têm um impacto muito grande sobre o transporte de mercadorias. O Brasil é um país grande e precisa transportar cargas por longas distâncias, isso afeta muito a produtividade do Brasil”, afirma Paulo Feldmann, da FEA-USP.

➡️ Países como Argentina e Estados Unidos também sofrem com a alta dos combustíveis, mas contam com redes ferroviárias que permitem escoar parte da produção agrícola e industrial por trens, diminuindo a dependência das rodovias em determinados trajetos.

Há também riscos para o abastecimento, como alertam os agricultores do RS. Murilo Viana, mestre em economia pela Universidade Estadual de Campinas (Unicamp), avalia que os subsídios concedidos recentemente pelo governo, ao manter os preços internos artificialmente abaixo dos internacionais, podem desestimular empresas privadas a importar diesel.

Nesse cenário, a Petrobras poderia ser pressionada a assumir uma parcela maior das importações, eventualmente vendendo o combustível com prejuízo por litro. Caso isso não ocorra, o país poderia enfrentar dificuldades de abastecimento por falta de importação pela iniciativa privada.

Como isso afeta os preços dos alimentos?

O agronegócio está entre os setores mais afetados pela alta do diesel, já que o combustível é utilizado tanto nas máquinas agrícolas, durante o preparo do solo, o plantio e a colheita, quanto no transporte da produção até armazéns, indústrias, portos e centros consumidores.

“O aumento dos custos pode reduzir a competitividade das exportações e encarecer os alimentos no mercado interno”, afirma Paulo Feldmann, da FEA-USP.

“Todos falam que 'da porteira para dentro' a agricultura brasileira é a mais competitiva do mundo. O Brasil perde muito no transporte, que é o que mais afeta o custo.”

Com o frete mais caro, produtores e empresas podem ter seus lucros reduzidos ou repassar parte dos custos adicionais aos compradores.

O repasse, porém, não acontece necessariamente de forma integral ou imediata. Parte do aumento pode ser absorvida ao longo da cadeia de produção e distribuição, dependendo dos contratos, da concorrência e das margens de lucro das empresas.

Nesse contexto, o governo Lula tem apostado em subsídios temporários para conter os efeitos de altas de preços que considera passageiras.

A prorrogação do subsídio anunciada pelo governo busca reduzir os efeitos da alta dos preços internacionais do petróleo no Brasil. Para Feldmann, a medida pode ajudar a conter o repasse dos custos, mas tem limites porque depende de recursos públicos, em um momento de dificuldades nas contas do governo.

Para Murilo Viana, o subsídio pode ser justificado pelo fato de que a alta dos preços internacionais do petróleo também pode elevar a arrecadação do governo brasileiro . Isso porque o país exporta petróleo bruto e recebe receitas de royalties, dividendos da Petrobras e tributos.

O subsídio, portanto, representa um gasto imediato para o governo, mas pode ajudar a evitar custos e impactos maiores sobre a economia. O resultado dessa estratégia, porém, depende de quanto o governo arrecada a mais com o petróleo, de quanto gasta com o subsídio e de quanto do aumento do diesel chegaria aos preços de outros produtos.

Para Viana, medidas para estabilizar os preços podem ser válidas, desde que sejam temporárias e tenham regras claras para seu encerramento , evitando que o subsídio se transforme em uma forma permanente de manter os preços artificialmente baixos.

O que reduziria a dependência brasileira?

Ampliar a capacidade de refino, investir em alternativas de transporte e reduzir a dependência de insumos importados são medidas que podem, na visão dos analistas, tornar o Brasil menos vulnerável.

Para Francismar Ferreira, do Ineep, uma solução de longo prazo exige ampliar e modernizar as refinarias brasileiras, além de aumentar os investimentos no setor.

A discussão também envolve o papel da Petrobras na produção de combustíveis derivados do petróleo, assim como na distribuição e revenda desses produtos.

O economista Murilo Viana também defende ampliar a produção nacional de fertilizantes, outro insumo essencial para o agronegócio.

Essa medida não resolve diretamente a dependência do diesel, mas faz parte de uma estratégia mais ampla para reduzir a vulnerabilidade do setor às oscilações do dólar e dos insumos no mercado internacional.

PEC Brasil movimenta o agronegócio em todo o país. — Foto: adobe stock

articles.title: India open to free, fair trade with China: Piyush Goyal
articles.summary: HAGUE: India is open to promoting free and fair trade with China and hopes to expand its exports of goods and services to the neighbouring country and
articles.body: HAGUE: India is open to promoting free and fair trade with China and hopes to expand its exports of goods and services to the neighbouring country and Asean region in the coming years, commerce and industry minister Piyush Goyal said late Monday, signalling scope for deeper trade engagement with Beijing.Goyal told reporters that India believed in open trade across the world and was looking for open markets in different countries on a reciprocal basis to sell Indian goods and services. “Yes, at some stage maybe we will do that also,” he said when asked if India was considering a similar exercise with China after concluding talks on a trade agreement with the European Union (EU).The minister said he had met his Chinese counterpart in Yaoundé, Cameroon, earlier this year and again in New Delhi during the latter’s visit for the Brics summit in Sept. “We are open to working and encouraging free and fair trade with every country around the globe. We are looking to open markets in different countries on a reciprocal basis for our goods and services also,” he said.As China supplies India with a number of critical intermediate goods and important raw materials, Goyal said there was an established judicial process that could be followed if it was ever found that the pricing of a particular good was not proper. “We believe in the rules of fair play, we believe in the rules of open trade across the world. Markets are open across the world. We welcome suppliers to meet the growing needs of India,” the minister said.Asked about China’s recent export controls on tunnelling equipment, which could impact several infrastructure projects, Goyal said he had learnt about the move after leaving India and that govt would work on the issue.According to commerce department data, China became India’s largest trading partner in the first half of the current fiscal year, with bilateral trade between the two countries rising 10.5% to $91.8 billion, with the trade deficit also expanding.While India has recently implemented trade deals with the UK and New Zealand and the EU agreement is expected to open markets in 27 European countries, Goyal said talks with Chile were nearing conclusion and those with Canada were making good progress. Mexico is keen on an “early-harvest” arrangement while negotiations with the South African Customs Union have just begun. He said India was working towards securing preferential access to economies accounting for 76% of the estimated $115 trillion global GDP.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Jio IPO Listing Live Updates: Ambani family seeks blessings at Mumbai’s Shree Siddhivinayak Temple after stel
articles.summary: Jio Platforms’ stock market debut was closely watched after its record-breaking initial public offering attracted bids worth billions of dollars and
articles.body: Jio platform share price: Jio Platforms Limited stock jumps over 23% Shares of Reliance Industries-backed Jio Platforms made a blockbuster stock market debut, rising nearly 23% over the issue price of Rs 1,119 and making the company India's second most valuable firm by market capitalisation. The stock listed at Rs 1,358 on both the BSE and NSE, marking a gain of 21.36% over the issue price. It later touched a high of Rs 1,375 on the BSE, up 22.87%, while on the NSE it climbed 22.83% to Rs 1,374.50. Jio Platforms' market valuation stood at Rs 12,57,401.07 crore..Jio Platforms listing: Akash Ambani says IPO 'response surpassed our imagination' Akash Ambani, chairman of Reliance Jio Infocomm, said the response to the IPO had exceeded the company’s expectations. The offering received demand worth more than Rs 7.5 lakh crore and over 1.3 crore applications. “The response surpassed our imagination, breaking records in every investor category. We were fully subscribed for India's largest IPO within 95 minutes of launch, the fastest ever India has seen,” he said. Ambani described the listing as the beginning of a new phase for the company, rather than an endpoint, and underlined its responsibility towards shareholders..Reliance Jio debuts today: Jio Platforms’ market capitalisation hits Rs 12.5 lakh crore Jio Platforms made a strong stock market debut with shares were trading at Rs 1,357.45, up Rs 238.45, or 21.31%, from the issue price. The stock touched an early high of Rs 1,374 before trading at around Rs 1,357. At these levels, Jio Platforms’ market capitalisation stood at around Rs 12.5 lakh crore. Reliance Industries, which holds a 64.48% stake in Jio Platforms, was trading at Rs 1,197 per share around 9.59 am, up 0.07% from its previous close of Rs 1,196.20. Speaking at the listing ceremony, Akash Ambani, chairman of Reliance Jio Infocomm, said the IPO had received demand worth more than Rs 7.5 lakh crore, along with over 1.3 crore applications, exceeding expectations..Jio Platforms debuts with 21% premium .Jio Platforms Limited debuts: Jio Platforms registers stellar opening at Dalal Street Shares of Jio Platforms, the country’s largest-ever public offering, made their stock market debut, listing at Rs 1,359 on the BSE and NSE, a 21.36% premium over the IPO price of Rs 1,119 per share. The Rs 30,200-crore IPO attracted cumulative demand of more than Rs 7 lakh crore across the anchor and public book-building process. Investor appetite was evident from the outset, with the issue being fully subscribed within 100 minutes of opening. The Rs 5,500-crore portion reserved for qualified institutional buyers (QIBs) was subscribed within the first 10 minutes..Jio Platforms listing: Jio Platforms makes strong debut, lists at 21% premium to issue price Jio Platforms Limited (JPL) made a strong stock market debut on the NSE and BSE, with premium of Rs 250, or 22.34%, over its issue price of Rs 1,119. The stock was 1369.00, up 11 points or 0.81% on both benchmarks..Reliance Jio IPO lists today: Jio Platforms to debut Dalal Street shortly Jio Platforms shares were indicated at Rs 1,358 in the pre-listing session, a premium of Rs 239, or 21.36%, over the issue price. The company’s $3.2 billion initial public offering was fully subscribed within 100 minutes of opening for bids on October 21, drawing strong investor demand for India’s biggest-ever share sale. The IPO also marked the first public offering from the Reliance group in two decades..Jai Shree Krishna…Let me begin with the one word that matters most today: gratitude. I am deeply grateful to the millions who believed in Jio and made this day possible. Thank you all from the bottom of my heart. Today, the bell at the stock exchange will ring for me like a temple bell. For me, business is a form of worship, and every worship ritual concludes with prasad. We offer this day at the feet of Lord Ganesha, Dwarkanath Ji, Shrinathji, Balaji, and the living goddess, Bharat Mata…Many years ago, a dream emerged from an ordinary home in Chorwad. It belonged to a young man who worked at a petrol pump in Aden, with neither money nor recognition. That young man was our revered Grandfather Dhirubhai Ambani. He showed us that an ordinary Indian can dream extraordinary dreams. .Jio IPO listing today: ‘Business is puja,’ Anant Ambani expresses gratitude at Jio Platforms listing Speaking at the listing ceremony of Jio Platforms Limited, Reliance Industries Executive Director Anant Ambani began by expressing gratitude to the millions who had believed in Jio and made the occasion possible. “Let me begin with the one word that matters the most today, gratitude, to the millions who believed in Jio and made this day possible. I express my heartfelt gratitude towards you all,” he said. Ambani added that the exchange bell held a special significance for him, likening its sound to a temple bell. “Today, the bell at the Exchange will ring for me as a temple bell because for me business is puja and every puja ends with prasad, and prasad is always shared,” he said..Reliance Jio IPO: Investors upbeat on Jio Platforms’ debut as they await for the biggest IPO As Jio Platforms Ltd makes its stock market debut, an investor said the excitement was palpable, describing it as the biggest IPO. “The stock got oversubscribed in a few minutes. I am sure that Jio will be at the forefront of the Indian success story driven by the youth of the country,” the investor said..NSE is proud to welcome Jio Platforms Limited. Jio Platforms Limited becomes the 12th company from Reliance Industries to list on NSE. NSE and Jio represent two important pillars of India's growth story. .Jio IPO listing today: Jio Platforms to debut on Dalal Street shortly .Reliance Jio listing: Jio Platforms shares indicate 21.36% premium in NSE pre-open session Jio Platforms shares were trading at Rs 1,358 in the NSE pre-open session, marking a premium of Rs 239, or 21.36%, over the issue price. The pre-open indication pointed to a substantial premium over the IPO issue price, as investors tracked the listing of the telecom and digital services company. The NSE data listed the security as Jio Platforms Limited, with the identifier INE0BJO01010..JIO IPO listing: When will Jio Platforms shares start trading on NSE and BSE? Jio Platforms is set to make its debut on the NSE and BSE at 10 am. Ahead of regular trading, the shares are expected to go through a special pre-open session, as prescribed under the standard equity-market listing process..JIO IPO listing: 22% GMP hints at a strong listing premium Jio Platforms’ IPO grey market premium (GMP) stood at Rs 248, indicating a premium of 22.2%. The mainboard issue had a price band of Rs 1,065 to Rs 1,119 per share, with a total issue size of Rs 30,187.65 crore. The grey market premium is an unofficial indicator and does not guarantee the price at which shares will list on the stock exchanges..Reliance JIO IPO listing: Jio Platforms eyes growth through AI, cloud computing and 6G technology Jio Platforms is looking to expand beyond telecom, with technology, artificial intelligence and cloud computing expected to drive its next phase of growth, the telecom giant's managing director Akash Ambani told PTI earlier. “There is no either-or at Jio: the network is our technology,” Ambani said, highlighting the company’s in-house 5G core, cloud-native radio access network and software platform, which serves 533.3 million customers. The company is also exploring satellite connectivity and next-generation 6G technology as areas for future development. Ambani said Jio’s growth opportunities span mobile services, home broadband and digital solutions for enterprises. He pointed to the scope for expansion, noting that around 26 crore Indians still use 2G services, while fixed broadband reaches only about 21% of households in the country..JIO IPO listing: QIB portion subscribed 70.55 times Qualified institutional buyers led the demand for Jio Platforms’ initial public offering, subscribing to their reserved portion 70.55 times. The non-institutional investor category was subscribed 14 times, while the retail investor portion was subscribed 2.72 times. The portions reserved for employees and Reliance Industries shareholders were subscribed around 2.93 times and 7.6 times, respectively. Overall, the IPO closed with subscriptions of 22.19 times the shares on offer. The category-wise figures show the level of demand across institutional, non-institutional, retail, employee and shareholder segments during the issue’s three-day subscription window..Jio IPO Listing: Mukesh Ambani’s plan to build an ‘everything company’ The listing of Jio Platforms furthers Mukesh Ambani’s plan to transform Reliance Industries from an oil-and-chemicals conglomerate into an “everything company” spanning consumer and technology businesses. Jio Platforms is Reliance Industries’ telecom and digital services unit and serves more than 530 million customers. Its initial public offering raised $3.2 billion and valued the company at up to $108.3 billion. The listing ceremony is expected to be attended by Akash Ambani, Mukesh Ambani’s eldest son and Jio Platforms’ managing director, according to an industry source with direct knowledge. The company’s stock market debut is scheduled for Wednesday, October 28..Reliance Jio IPO: Reliance shares deliver around 900% returns in two decades Over the last two decades, Reliance shares have delivered returns of around 900%, outperforming the benchmark Nifty index’s 685% return over the same period, according to LSEG data. Jio Platforms, the company’s telecom and digital services unit, is now set to make its stock market debut following its $3.2 billion IPO. The issue attracted strong demand, closing with subscriptions of 22.19 times the shares on offer. Jio Platforms is valued at up to $108.3 billion ahead of its listing on Wednesday, October 28..Reliance Jio IPO: Investor demand build rapidly from day 1 Jio Platforms’ IPO was fully subscribed within the first 100 minutes of opening on October 21. The rapid response continued over the three-day bidding period, with the issue subscribed more than five times by Day 2 before closing at 22.19 times on October 23. In most Indian IPOs, subscription levels typically build gradually, with institutional investors often placing bids closer to the deadline. Jio Platforms’ offering saw substantial demand from the beginning of the subscription period. The issue was priced in a band of Rs 1,065 to Rs 1,119 per share, with a lot size of 12 shares..JIO IPO listing: India ranks first by IPO deal count this year India has become the world’s busiest initial public offering market this year by the number of deals, with 246 listings so far. However, it ranks fourth by the amount of money raised, at $13.5 billion, behind the United States, mainland China and Hong Kong, according to LSEG data. Jio Platforms’ $3.2 billion offering is India’s largest IPO and attracted bids worth $77 billion. The listing is being closely watched as a test of investor appetite for large public offerings amid increased scrutiny of artificial intelligence-linked stocks. Several brokerages have described Jio Platforms’ $108.3 billion valuation as attractive, while flagging competition, heavy capital spending and changes in telecom rules as risks. .Reliance Jio IPO: ADIA, BlackRock and Fidelity among investors Jio Platforms’ initial public offering received substantial demand from anchor investors, including the Abu Dhabi Investment Authority, BlackRock and Fidelity. The $854 million worth of shares reserved for these investors received bids exceeding $25 billion on Monday, according to the provided inputs. The anchor investor response preceded the three-day public subscription period, during which the issue attracted around 1.3 crore applications. The $3.2 billion IPO was fully subscribed within its first 100 minutes and closed with overall subscriptions of 22.19 times. Total demand, including the anchor investor portion, approached Rs 7.5 lakh crore, according to reports..Jio IPO Listing: GMP indicates blockbuster 22% premium Ahead of Jio Platforms’ stock market debut, the grey-market premium indicated potential listing gains of about 22%. The grey market is an unregulated market in which investors trade in shares before they are listed on the stock exchanges. The premium is an indication of the price at which unlisted shares are being traded relative to the IPO price. Jio Platforms’ issue was priced between Rs 1,065 and Rs 1,119 per share, with the upper end of the price band at Rs 1,119. However, the grey-market premium does not establish the actual listing price. The company’s market debut on Wednesday will determine its listing price..Reliance Jio IPO: Jio IPO attracts around 1.3 crore applications Jio Platforms’ initial public offering became the first public issue globally to receive more than one crore applications. The issue attracted around 1.3 crore applications, according to reports, as demand surged during the three-day bidding period. The $3.2 billion offering drew interest from institutional and retail investors, employees and shareholders. Subscription levels rose sharply after the IPO opened on October 21 and closed on October 23. The issue was subscribed 22.19 times overall, while total demand, including the anchor investor portion, approached Rs 7.5 lakh crore, according to reports..Jio IPO listing: Jio Platforms set for stock market debut Jio Platforms, the telecom and digital services unit of billionaire Mukesh Ambani’s Reliance Industries, is set to list on the stock exchanges on October 28. The company’s $3.2 billion initial public offering has become India’s largest public issue, attracting strong interest from institutional and retail investors, employees and Reliance Industries shareholders. Jio Platforms is valued at up to $108.3 billion, potentially making it one of India’s biggest companies by market capitalisation when trading begins. The listing follows a three-day subscription period from October 21 to October 23, during which the issue was subscribed 22.19 times overall.

articles.title: Government takes step to ease GST notices, litigation
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Following up on GST Council decisions, Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs has issued over half a dozen detailed circulars on steps to
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Following up on GST Council decisions, Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs has issued over half a dozen detailed circulars on steps to reduce litigation and appeals, issuing show cause notices to taxpayers and speeding up registrations and changes that businesses need to make. In addition, it has sought to address concerns around exports as well as sectoral issues such as those related to banks and NBFCs.Tax authorities have underlined the need to facilitate registration while ensuring that there is no misuse. “While there is a need to exercise due diligence in processing registration application to prevent GST registration form being obtained by unscrupulous and fraudulent elements for passing on input tax credit (ITC) without any underlying supply, at the same time, it is also important to ensure that genuine applicants seeking registration are able to complete the process without undue inconvenience,” CBIC said in the circular, while pointing to grievances that it had received due to difficulties faced by taxpayers.It specifies that pre-show cause notice intimation may be given to taxpayers, wherever feasible, so that they can clarify their position prior to the start of formal proceedings.You use AI every day. articles.title: Oil price today: Brent crude holds firm at $115 per barrel, WTI trades at $100
articles.summary: Oil prices edged higher again on Wednesday, with Brent crude crossing $115 a barrel after declining in previous sessions.
articles.body: Oil prices edged higher again on Wednesday, with Brent crude crossing $115 a barrel after declining in previous sessions. The rebound came after Yemen’s Iran-aligned Houthi group claimed a missile strike on Saudi Arabia’s largest oil refinery, reviving concerns over oil supplies from the Middle East amid the ongoing conflict involving Iran and its proxies.Brent crude gained $1.22, or 1.07%, to trade at $115.10, while US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude rose $0.96, or 0.96%, to $100.90.The Houthis on Tuesday said that they targeted the refinery, which has a processing capacity of 550,000 barrels per day. The claimed strike marked an escalation in their attacks against Saudi Arabia, the world's second-largest crude producer. Saudi authorities had not immediately confirmed the attack.The latest gains followed a decline of nearly $2 in oil prices on Tuesday, when talks in the Middle East helped ease concerns over supply disruptions. The reported strike brought those concerns back into focus.Expectations of higher crude inventories in the US provided another factor for the oil market to consider. US crude stockpiles increased by around 15,000 barrels in the week ended October 23, according to a Reuters poll of eight analysts.On the production front, OPEC+ members are expected to maintain their December oil output targets at Sunday's meeting, three people with knowledge of the matter told Reuters. The expected decision is in line with market expectations.Output in most of the group's seven core members, Saudi Arabia, Russia, Iraq, Kuwait, Algeria, Kazakhstan and Oman, is already below their respective production targets.Meanwhile, Russia's crude oil shipments from its Baltic and Black Sea ports could decrease next month, traders said.The potential decline comes as Russian domestic refiners prepare to increase diesel production following a deal with Washington this month.Oil prices have remained volatile as the Middle East crisis enters its eighth month. However, the latest spike remains below the $126-per-barrel peak recorded earlier in the crisis.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Jio share price: JPL makes strong debut at 21% premium; becomes India's second-most valuable firm - all you need to know
articles.summary: Jio stock price: Jio Platforms made a strong stock market debut on Wednesday, with its shares listing at Rs 1,358 on the BSE and NSE, a premium of around
articles.body: Jio stock price: Jio Platforms made a strong stock market debut on Wednesday, with its shares listing at Rs 1,358 on the BSE and NSE, a premium of around 21.35% over the issue price of Rs 1,119. The stock touched a high of Rs 1,375 and a low of Rs 1,356.40 during early trade. The listing comes after a record-breaking initial public offering (IPO) that attracted substantial demand from institutional and retail investors.The debut placed Jio Platforms among India's most valuable listed companies, with a market capitalisation of around Rs 12.5 lakh crore. It became the country's second most valuable company by market valuation, behind parent Reliance Industries. The IPO attracted bids worth more than Rs 7.4 lakh crore across the public issue and anchor investor placement, while applications approached 1.39 crore.Jio Platforms listing: All you need to knowStellar listingJio Platforms listed on the BSE and NSE at Rs 1,358 per share, around 21.35% above its issue price of Rs 1,119. During early trade, the stock touched a high of Rs 1,375 and a low of Rs 1,356.40.Its market valuation stood at Rs 12,50,586.39 crore during early deals on the BSE, placing it second in India's market capitalisation rankings, behind Reliance Industries.The top five companies by market capitalisation were:Reliance Industries: Rs 15.89 lakh croreJio Platforms: Rs 12.50 lakh croreBharti Airtel: Rs 12.05 lakh croreHDFC Bank: Rs 10.42 lakh croreICICI Bank: Rs 9.80 lakh croreThe combined market valuation of Jio Platforms and Reliance Industries stood at Rs 28.40 lakh crore.Blockbuster IPO attracted bids worth over Rs 7.4 lakh croreJio Platforms' Rs 30,213 crore IPO closed with bids for 22.19 times the shares on offer. Total demand across the public issue and anchor investor placement crossed Rs 7.4 lakh crore, while applications approached 1.39 crore.The offering was entirely a fresh issue of 27 crore shares, with the price band set at Rs 1,065 to Rs 1,119 per share. The IPO opened on October 21 and closed on October 23.Jio Platforms' IPO was fully subscribed within 100 minutes of opening, making it the fastest-subscribed mega public issue in India. At the listing ceremony, managing director Akash Ambani said the offering had been fully subscribed within 95 minutes of launch.“The response surpassed our imagination, breaking records in every investor category. We were fully subscribed for India's largest IPO within 95 minutes of launch, the fastest ever India has seen,” he said.The IPO's Rs 8,110 crore anchor book attracted institutional demand of more than Rs 2.5 lakh crore, exceeding the amount on offer by over 30 times.Bids from qualified institutional buyers reached 70.55 times the shares reserved for their category, contributing to the issue's overall subscription of 22.19 times.Grey market premium indicated a strong listingAhead of the listing, Jio Platforms shares were quoting at a grey market premium (GMP) of around 22%. On Tuesday, October 20, the premium stood at about Rs 245.Based on the upper end of the IPO price band of Rs 1,119, this indicated a possible listing price of Rs 1,364, implying a premium of nearly 22%, according to unofficial grey market quotes.GMP refers to the premium speculators in the unofficial market are prepared to pay for shares of a company awaiting its IPO listing.Speaking at the listing ceremony, Akash Ambani said that the response to the IPO had exceeded expectations. He pledged to take the company forward alongside his siblings, Isha and Anant.“We promise to take Jio to greater heights of growth, excellence, and reputation in India and the world,” he said.Ambani described the listing as the beginning of a new phase for the company and emphasised its responsibility towards its new shareholders.“Today's listing, as Isha said, is not a finish line, but a starting line. We will communicate openly, honor our commitments and earn your trust through our actions,” he said.Jio's future ambitionsSpeaking at the listing ceremony, Akash Ambani said that Jio aims to democratise technology with the potential to transform Indian lives over the next ten years, including through connectivity from space. The company's ambition, he added, is to build a digital society with Jio Platforms at its core, where connectivity, computing and intelligence work together seamlessly.Ambani said the company would continue to focus on expanding digital access and creating value for customers and investors. He also said the next generation of Ambanis had a responsibility to make Jio bigger, better and more meaningful for India, rather than merely preserve what they had inherited.Jio's homegrown platforms now serve more than 540 million customers, Ambani said, adding that the company would seek to build on its digital infrastructure and services.“As trustees of your wealth, our duty is to protect it, grow it decade after decade. The only way is by creating disproportionate value for our customers,” he said.The listing ceremony was attended by Akash Ambani's parents, Mukesh Ambani and Nita Ambani, along with his siblings and grandmother, Kokilaben.You use AI every day. articles.title: Mukesh Ambani gets teary-eyed as Anant, Akash, Isha talk about Reliance's journey at Jio listing
articles.summary: Jio share listing: Reliance Industries chairman Mukesh Ambani got emotional at Jio Platforms Limited’s listing ceremony as he watched his children speak
articles.body: Jio share listing: Reliance Industries chairman Mukesh Ambani got emotional at Jio Platforms Limited’s listing ceremony as he watched his children speak about the family’s legacy and Jio’s journey. Sitting beside his wife, Nita Ambani, the 69-year-old chairman listened as Isha, Akash and Anant Ambani addressed the gathering ahead of the NSE bell-ringing ceremony.The occasion was particularly significant for Reliance, marking its first listing in two decades with the stock market debut of Jio Platforms Limited. The ceremony brought together the company’s history, the contribution of its founders and the responsibility its next generation now carries.Jio Platforms made a strong debut on Dalal Street, listing at Rs 1,359 on the BSE and NSE, a premium of 21.36% over its IPO issue price of Rs 1,119 per share. The Rs 30,213-crore public issue was subscribed 22.19 times, making it India's largest IPO to date and valuing the Reliance Industries-backed digital services business at over Rs 10 lakh crore.Isha Ambani recalls father's early days at RelianceIsha Ambani, executive director of Reliance Retail Ventures, took the gathering back to the company's beginnings, recalling a recent family dinner during which her father spoke about Reliance's first public offering in 1977. Mukesh Ambani was 20 at the time, while his father, Dhirubhai Ambani, had decided to take the company to the public."A few evenings ago, at our dinner table, my father, Shri Mukesh Ambani, was remembering his days in 1977. He was 20 years old, working on Reliance's first public offering. My grandfather, Shri Dhirubhai Ambani, had decided to take Reliance to the people," she said.Isha also recalled the maxim associated with her grandfather, 'Growth is life', and vowed to continue building the business and creating value for shareholders. She said Akash had worked hard for 13 years to build and grow Jio into India's largest telecom company, with over 53 crore subscribers.Isha planted Jio's idea, says brother AnantAnant Ambani, executive director of Reliance Industries, recalled how Jio grew from an idea planted by his sister Isha and nurtured by her twin brother, Akash. Reflecting on Reliance’s journey and its global ambitions, he said, “Once-barren land of Jamnagar turned into the site of the world's largest refinery. He showed the world that when India builds, the world takes notice. Then came the New India, the young India, and a new dream: internet in every hand and the world within reach of every village. The name of that dream was Jio. The seed of this dream was planted by Isha Didi, and Akash Bhai made that seed his own dream. Jio was then taken to every corner of the country.”The ceremony also highlighted the scale of investor interest in the company. Akash said that the IPO received demand worth Rs 7.5 lakh crore through 1.3 crore applications, with the issue fully subscribed within 95 minutes of its launch. He described the response as deeply humbling and said it had left him with a profound sense of responsibility.The entire Ambani family, including the next generation, rang the bell as the clock struck 10 am. By 11.01 am, Jio Platforms shares were trading 21.42% higher at Rs 1,358.7 on the BSE, against a 0.89% decline in the benchmark index.Akash Ambani calls listing a ‘start line’Jio Platforms managing director Akash Ambani said the listing was not a finish line but a start line. He promised to take the company to greater heights and grow investor wealth, as Reliance Industries has done over nearly 50 years."We promise to take Jio to greater heights of growth, excellence and reputation in India and the world," the 35-year-old said at the NSE ceremony, attended by his parents, siblings and grandmother Kokilaben.Akash said the next generation's responsibility was not simply to preserve what it had inherited, but to make Jio bigger, better and more meaningful for India.He said Jio had democratised data in its first decade and would now focus on making more technologies accessible."In our next ten (years), we want to democratise every technology that can transform Indian lives: AI, cloud, connected devices, connectivity even from space and digital services not yet imagined," he said.Akash described the company's ambition as building a digital society where connectivity, computing and intelligence work together seamlessly. He said India was emerging as a creator of technology rather than merely a consumer. "We are now ready to take the tricolour global", he added.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: Jio marks historic NSE debut after breaking India's IPO records in just 95 minutes
articles.summary: Marking a watershed moment for Indian capital markets, Reliance Industries' digital and telecommunications arm, Jio Platforms Limited, made a blockbuster
articles.body: Marking a watershed moment for Indian capital markets, Reliance Industries' digital and telecommunications arm, Jio Platforms Limited, made a blockbuster debut on the National Stock Exchange on 28 October. In a grand ceremony that showcased a generational shift, the entire Ambani family, led by Mukesh and Nita Ambani, alongside the third generation of leaders, rang the ceremonial bell to officially list the technology giant.The stock debuted at Rs 1,358 to Rs 1,360 on the NSE, reflecting strong investor confidence as the benchmark Nifty50 traded near 22,591. The listing follows a historic initial public offering that shattered domestic records.Record-breaking demandAddressing the gathering, Akash Ambani revealed the unprecedented scale of the public issue. He announced that India's largest IPO was fully subscribed within just 95 minutes of its launch, making it the fastest in the country's history."We garnered over Rs 7.5 lakh crore of demand, the highest ever India has seen," Akash Ambani said. "And over 1.3 crore Indians trusted us with their wealth, the highest ever application count India has seen."He noted that when the project began, the company had zero revenue and zero customers. Today, the platform serves over 540 million users."My dream is that one day, when the world counts its great technology companies, one of them will be from India, and that company will be called Jio Platforms Limited," he added.Legacy and social impactThe ceremony heavily emphasised the theme "Thank you, India. Jio aapne banaya." Isha Ambani drew a historical parallel to the year 1977, when a 20-year-old Mukesh Ambani assisted founder Dhirubhai Ambani in taking Reliance public. That issue raised Rs 2.82 crore at a Rs 10 crore valuation from ordinary citizens."Almost 50 years later, that trust has come full circle," Isha Ambani said. She highlighted the company's financial strength, noting that this year Jio earned about USD 15.5 billion in revenue and USD 8 billion in real earnings.Anant Ambani anchored his speech on the social and emotional impact of digital connectivity, dedicating the milestone to the 53 crore members of the Jio family."Today, the bell at the Exchange will ring for me like a temple bell," Anant Ambani said. "Because for me, business is Puja. And every Puja ends with Prasad. Prasad is always shared. Today, Jio is shared with India."He highlighted how the network empowered rural citizens, students, and soldiers, serving as the invisible backbone for India's digital aspirations. He also underscored the unity among the third generation of leadership."Today, Isha Didi, Akash Bhai, and I stand before you as three bodies, but one soul, with one commitment: to honour these dreams," he said.The listing brings a massive influx of fresh capital directly onto the company's balance sheet. With zero existing investors selling their stakes in the offering, the proceeds will be used to prepay debt and fuel future growth across artificial intelligence, cloud, and next-generation digital services.You use AI every day. articles.title: Stock market today: Dow futures fall, S&P 500 and Nasdaq futures climb ahead of Fed decision, Big Tech earnings
articles.summary: A critical day for markets arrives, with a Fed decision and earnings results from Microsoft and Alphabet.
articles.body: US stock futures were mixed ahead of a critical day for markets, with a Fed decision and earnings results from Microsoft (MSFT) and Alphabet (GOOG) on deck.Futures on the Dow Jones Industrial Average (YM=F) declined by 0.3%, while those on the S&P 500 (ES=F) traded above the flat line, and contracts for the tech-heavy Nasdaq-100 (NQ=F) rose 0.3%.Sentiment in the tech trade has markedly improved this week, with the S&P 500 and Nasdaq posting back-to-back gains. Semiconductor stocks drove the rally on Tuesday after Broadcom's CEO negotiated for a consortium of banks to announce a $63 billion financing structure for building AI compute capacity.Attention now turns toward the Federal Reserve's interest rate decision at 2 p.m. ET, where the Fed is expected to hold rates steady despite elevated inflation readings. Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh's press conference will be closely watched for any signs of a hawkish bias. (Follow live updates from the meeting.)Earnings season continues apace as two Big Tech giants and cloud leaders — Microsoft and Alphabet — deliver updates on AI demand and their capex plans after the bell. Microsoft's report comes just after it offered buyouts to up to 60,000 employees as it tries to streamline operations amid the AI build-out.Rounding out the earnings picture are Ford (F), GE Vernova (GEV), T-Mobile US (TMUS), eBay (EBAY), Chipotle Mexican Grill (CMG), and ServiceNow (NOW).

articles.title: Maruti profit declines 27% despite record quarterly sales
articles.summary: New Delhi: Record vehicle sales could not shield Maruti Suzuki from a sharp fall in quarterly profit as higher costs and investment losses squeezed
articles.body: New Delhi: Record vehicle sales could not shield Maruti Suzuki from a sharp fall in quarterly profit as higher costs and investment losses squeezed earnings. India's largest carmaker reported standalone net profit of Rs 2,415 crore for July-Sept, down 27% year-on-year. Net sales rose 26% to a record Rs 50,616 crore, while vehicle sales increased 26.5% to an all-time quarterly high of over 6.9 lakh units.The earnings decline came as commodity inflation linked to West Asia disruptions pushed up costs. Total expenditure rose nearly 30% to Rs 50,604 crore, outpacing sales growth.Raw material and component expenditure increased 48% to Rs 37,488 crore amid higher production volumes and cost pressures. Operating profit fell 17% to Rs 2,804 crore from Rs 3,382 crore a year earlier.Mark-to-market losses on invested surplus added to the pressure, pulling non-operating income down to Rs 430 crore from Rs 966 crore.Demand remained strong, with small-car sales rising 35.9% and utility vehicle volumes growing 68.2%.Exports, however, declined to 1.08 lakh vehicles from 1.1 lakh vehicles in the corresponding quarter last year.Standalone revenue from operations, including servicing and ancillary income, increased to Rs 53,340 crore from Rs 42,332 crore. Consolidated net profit fell 26% to Rs 2,466 crore, while consolidated revenue reached Rs 53,356 crore. For April-Sept, standalone net profit declined 18% to Rs 5,767 crore from Rs 7,061 crore, reflecting sustained pressure on earnings despite the expansion in sales.You use AI every day.
